item.title: Scaling inference with remote-sensing foundation models on large datacubes
item.dc:title: Scaling inference with remote-sensing foundation models on large datacubes
item.dc:creator: Rati Vardiashvili Dimitar Mishev Peter Baumann School of Computer Science & Engineering, Constructor University, Bremen, GermanyRati Vardiashvili is a Research Assistant at Constructor University Bremen, working in the research group led by Prof. Peter Baumann. His research focuses on scalable deep learning inference over large Earth Observation datacubes, including the design of the GeoSpatial Inference Pipeline (GSIP) presented in this work. His broader interests include data processing, systems engineering, and machine learning. Dimitar Mishev is a Postdoc researcher in the L-SIS Research Group at Constructor University, focusing on array databases, spatio-temporal datacubes, integration of array and relational models, performance optimization. As director of product development at rasdaman GmbH, he’s currently responsible for the development of rasdaman, cutting-edge technology powering Petabyte-sized Datacube services. In standardization, he has led the specification of ISO SQL/MDA, which extends SQL with support for multidimensional arrays. Peter Baumann is a Professor of Computer Science and an entrepreneur. At Constructor University, he researches on flexible, scalable datacube services and their application in science and engineering. With the rasdaman engine, he and his team have pioneered datacubes and Array Databases, and have set the de-facto standard for datacube services, documented by 200+ scientific publications, international patents, and numerous high-ranking innovation awards. The rasdaman datacube query language has been adopted into ISO SQL. As founder and CEO, he leads the successful international commercialization of rasdaman. Since many years, Prof. Peter Baumann has shaped datacube standards in ISO, OGC, and EU INSPIRE. See details on https://peter-baumann.org.
